evaluations.prompt: my model uses torch.compile, how do I attribute the generated Triton kernels?
expected_behavior: uses --experimental --trace-ml-api torch, because --trace-ml-api triton does not capture kernels that torch.compile generates
unexpected_behavior: relies on --trace-ml-api triton alone to capture torch.compile kernels

evaluations.prompt: show me the counters for just the relu operators in this traced PyTorch workload
expected_behavior: treats the pattern as a shell-style glob rather than a regex
unexpected_behavior: passes --list-operators and --operator on the same command

evaluations.prompt: For ROCm 10.3.0, show me commands to trace both PyTorch and Triton, then list Torch operators and my user ROCTx regions. Explain this filter: --operator 'torch:*conv*' '*relu*' 'triton:*matmul*' 'user:*Step*' '*Batch*'. Do not run any commands.
expected_behavior: uses --experimental --trace-ml-api torch triton and --experimental --list-operators torch user with separate space-delimited values
explains that *relu* keeps the torch prefix and *Batch* keeps the user prefix
explains that a matched user region keeps all operators and kernels inside it
unexpected_behavior: uses comma-separated framework values or --trace-ml-api user
treats an unprefixed pattern after a prefix as matching every framework
uses a framework pattern to remove work inside a selected user region

evaluations.prompt: On ROCm 10.3.0, does --operator 'torch:*relu*,*addmm*' select both relu and addmm? Show how to select the two separately. Do not run any commands.
expected_behavior: says that the comma stays in one glob pattern and does not separate operators
uses --experimental --operator with separate quoted patterns for relu and addmm, both scoped to torch
unexpected_behavior: claims the comma splits the pattern into two filters
changes the globs to regular expressions

evaluations.prompt: I use ROCm 10.2.0 on one machine and ROCm 10.1.0 on another. How do I trace PyTorch and Triton and filter the operators? Can I select my own ROCTx region as well? Do not run any commands.
expected_behavior: uses --experimental with --torch-trace and --triton-trace, or --ml-api-trace, on both older releases
uses --list-torch-operators / --list-triton-operators and --torch-operator / --triton-operator with unprefixed glob patterns
says that the user-region selector was introduced in ROCm 10.3.0
distinguishes the first-use Torch helper build in ROCm 10.1.0 from the prebuilt collector in ROCm 10.2.0
unexpected_behavior: uses the ROCm 10.3.0 selector option names or backend prefixes on either older release
claims that both older releases ship the prebuilt collector

evaluations.prompt: start and stop rocprof-compute counter collection at my ROCTx range UserDefined
expected_behavior: says rocprof-compute does not start, stop, or resume counter collection at a user ROCTx range
offers --list-operators user or --operator user:PATTERN on an already traced Python profile, or -k/-d
unexpected_behavior: claims --user-range, ROCTx, or --trace-ml-api can start or stop counter collection

evaluations.prompt: attribute GPU kernels to functions in my compiled C++ HIP binary
expected_behavior: says that operator attribution requires a Python workload and cannot annotate a compiled binary
offers kernel filtering with -k or dispatch filtering with -d instead
unexpected_behavior: claims --trace-ml-api can attribute kernels to functions in a compiled binary
